name: Liu Shen-hsu
bio: Liu Shen-hsu was a T'ang poet who flourished about AD 742–755. His poem here is printed in the book with the note that its title is lost.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu's versions in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet's name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Poem
poems.author: Liu Shen-hsu
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
On a road outreaching the white clouds,
By a spring outrunning the bluest river,
Petals come drifting on the wind
And the brook is sweet with them all the way.
My quiet gate is a mountain-trail,
And the willow-trees about my cottage
Sift on my sleeve, through the shadowy noon,
Distillations of the sun.
